candidate.title: Adds the `global.rbac.disableHTTPChallengesRole` helm value to disable HTTP-01 ACME challenges
candidate.text:
Adds the `global.rbac.disableHTTPChallengesRole` helm value to disable HTTP-01 ACME challenges. This allows cert-manager to drop its permission to create pods, improving security when HTTP-01 challenges are not required. (`#7666`, `@ali-hamza-noor`)
- computed artifact diff (values:added): New Helm value `global.rbac.disableHTTPChallengesRole`; subjects: global.rbac.disableHTTPChallengesRole — Defaults in v1.18.0: global.rbac.disableHTTPChallengesRole = false # To use HTTP-01 ACME challenges, cert-manager needs extra permissions to create pods. If you want to avoid this added permission and disable HTTP-01 set this value.

PR: More fine-grained control over powerful RBAC permission granted via Helm chart [closed; labels release-note, approved, lgtm, kind/feature, size/M, dco-signoff: yes, ok-to-test, area/deploy]
### Pull Request Motivation

This open [issue](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/7598) highlights that the ClusterRole `...-controller-challenges` would be able to create arbitrary pods in any namespace which means that an attacker who compromised the cert-manager controller could probably escalate their privileges to cluster-admin level. For this reason some people deploy their own ro…

to deploy all the roles on their own. This PR provides a more fine-grained way of turning off the challenger role only.

### Kind

/kind feature

### Release Note

```release-note
Adds the `global.rbac.disableHTTPChallengesRole` helm value to disable HTTP-01 ACME challenges. This allows cert-manager to drop its permission to create pods, improving security when HTTP-01 challenges are not required.
```
